title: Real-Time Data Pipelines
tagline: The end-to-end path data takes from the moment it's generated to the moment it's acted on.
what_it_is: A real-time data pipeline is the full chain of systems that captures data as it's generated, moves it (often via a tool like Kafka), processes it (often via a stream processing engine like Spark Structured Streaming), and delivers results to a dashboard, alert system, or downstream application — all within seconds.
key_points: Typically follows a pattern: source event → ingestion (Kafka) → stream processing (Spark Streaming/Flink) → sink (dashboard, database, alert system).
Latency (time from event to result) is the key metric that defines whether a pipeline is 'real-time' enough for its use case.
Must handle out-of-order and late-arriving data gracefully — network delays mean events don't always arrive in the order they happened.
Fault tolerance and exactly-once processing guarantees are critical — losing or duplicating events can silently corrupt downstream decisions.
Monitoring pipeline health (consumer lag, processing delays) is an ongoing operational responsibility, unlike a batch job that just runs and finishes.
why_it_exists: Individually, streaming tools like Kafka and Spark Streaming only solve one piece of the puzzle. Real-time pipelines exist as the end-to-end architecture pattern connecting ingestion, processing, and delivery into one coherent, continuously running system that turns raw events into timely action.
intuition: Think of an air traffic control system: radar signals (events) stream in continuously, get processed instantly to calculate positions and potential collisions, and get displayed on a controller's screen within seconds — not compiled into a report reviewed the next morning. The pipeline is the entire chain from raw radar signal to the controller's live screen.
when_to_use: Use real-time pipelines when a business decision or user experience genuinely depends on data being seconds old, not hours old.
Use them for live dashboards, fraud detection, real-time recommendations, or operational alerting.
when_not_to_use: Do not build a full real-time pipeline when a nightly batch job would satisfy the actual business need — it adds significant operational complexity and cost.
Do not treat 'real-time' as a marketing requirement rather than an actual latency need dictated by the use case.
common_mistakes: Not planning for late or out-of-order events, leading to subtly incorrect real-time aggregations.
Underestimating the ongoing operational burden — real-time pipelines need 24/7 monitoring, unlike a batch job that runs and finishes.
Skipping exactly-once processing guarantees, leading to double-counted events during failures and retries.
ds_usage: The architecture behind fraud detection systems, live operational dashboards, real-time personalization/recommendation engines, and IoT sensor monitoring — anywhere a delayed answer is a wrong answer.
